base_value_source: FY2025 Adj. EBITDA (company-defined, non-GAAP) [`01_historical-financials.md` §1, citing Financials.xls Segments tab, 'Total EBITDA' row]

sensitivities.label: Consolidated revenue YoY growth rate (proxy for Mobility Gross Bookings growth, the largest revenue driver)
sensitivities.non_linearity: Coefficient uses the FY2024->FY2025 average incremental EBITDA margin (~27.9% = $2,246mm EBITDA gain / $8,039mm revenue gain). In a deceleration this likely overstates margin retention because SG&A/R&D are semi-fixed near-term (operating deleverage), so the true bear-case EBITDA hit could exceed the linear estimate.
sensitivities.source: Derived from `01_historical-financials.md` §1 (FY2024/FY2025 Revenue and Adj. EBITDA). Inference, not from filings.

sensitivities.label: Cost of revenue (COGS) as % of revenue, in bps (driven mainly by the insurance-cost / driver-incentive line)
sensitivities.non_linearity: Insurance-cost savings are currently fully reinvested into pricing per management, not banked - zero disclosed margin buffer, so an adverse (bear) move is not offset by any other cost lever; asymmetric downside versus the bull case.
sensitivities.source: `03_margin-drivers.md` §3-4, §8 (COGS ratio FY2024 62.49% -> FY2025 61.50%, Financials.xls Income Statement tab); move-size basis is the historical one-year observed change.

sensitivities.label: SG&A as % of revenue, in bps (AI-driven headcount-discipline lever)
sensitivities.non_linearity: LTM SG&A ratio (20.50%) has already partially reversed +63bps versus the FY2025 endpoint (19.87%), showing this lever can move against the company within two quarters, faster than the multi-year improving trend would suggest.
sensitivities.source: `03_margin-drivers.md` §3-4, §6 (SG&A ratio FY2024 22.45% -> FY2025 19.87%, LTM 20.50%, Financials.xls Income Statement tab).
